- **Timeline:** 2–4 days depending on weather and access

- **Timeline:** 1–3 days depending on roof size and pitch

### Pricing Questions

**How much does house painting cost in Melbourne?**
Interior painting typically costs $30–$60 per square metre depending on prep, coats, and paint spec. A full interior repaint of a 3-bedroom home typically ranges from $4,000–$9,000. Exterior painting for a single-storey weatherboard home starts around $4,500–$7,500. Roof painting typically costs $2,500–$6,000. All quotes are free and itemised in writing.

**How much does exterior house painting cost in Melbourne?**
Exterior painting costs depend on the home's size, surface type (weatherboard, render, brick), prep required, and storeys. A single-storey weatherboard home typically starts around $4,500–$7,500. A double-storey home is typically $8,000–$15,000. All surface preparation (pressure washing, sanding, filling, priming) is included.

**How much does kitchen cabinet resurfacing cost?**
Kitchen cabinet resurfacing with a 2-pack spray finish typically costs $2,500–$6,000 depending on the number of doors, drawer fronts and whether shelving is included. This is a fraction of the cost of replacing cabinets, which typically costs $15,000–$40,000+.

**How much does roof painting cost in Melbourne?**
Roof painting in Melbourne typically costs $2,500–$6,000 for a standard residential roof, depending on size, pitch, condition and whether repairs are needed. Jetblack Painting includes pressure cleaning, crack repair, priming, and quality roof coatings in every roof painting quote.

**How much does commercial painting cost?**
Commercial painting costs vary by project size and scope. Small office repaints (500m²) typically cost $2,000–$5,000. Large retail or industrial projects (2,000m²+) typically cost $8,000–$25,000+. After-hours and weekend scheduling carries a 10–20% premium. Free detailed quotes provided.

### Timeline Questions

**How long does a house painting job take?**
A typical 3-bedroom interior repaint takes 3–5 days. An exterior repaint takes 2–4 days depending on access, prep, and weather conditions. Kitchen cabinet resurfacing typically takes 2–3 days. Roof painting takes 1–3 days depending on roof size and pitch.

**How long does interior painting take?**
Most interior painting projects take 3–7 days depending on the size and complexity. A single room typically takes 1–2 days. A full 3-bedroom home typically takes 3–5 days. A detailed timeline is provided during your free quote.

**How long does exterior painting take?**
Exterior painting typically takes 2–4 days depending on home size, surface condition, weather, and access. Surface preparation (pressure washing, sanding, repairs) often takes as long as the painting itself — all included in your quote.

**What's the best time of year to paint in Melbourne?**
Exterior painting is best done between October and April when conditions are drier and warmer. Avoid days below 10°C or above 35°C, and high-humidity days, since they affect how paint cures. Interior painting can be done year-round.

### Quality & Guarantee Questions

**What guarantee does Jetblack Painting offer?**
Every job is backed by a 5-year written workmanship guarantee. If anything related to Jetblack Painting's workmanship fails within 5 years, they return to fix it at no cost. This covers peeling, flaking, poor adhesion, and paint defects.

**What paint brands does Jetblack Painting use?**
Jetblack Painting uses premium Australian paint brands — primarily Dulux and Taubmans — selecting the right product for each surface and environment. For coastal homes, products rated for salt air and UV resistance are used. Exact product recommendations are provided in your quote.

**How do you protect coastal homes from salt air damage?**
Salt air deposits on surfaces, breaks down paint adhesion and accelerates rust on metal trim — causing paint to fail in 2–3 years if poorly prepared. Jetblack Painting counters this with thorough salt-air washing, flexible primers rated for coastal use, and premium topcoats formulated for salt air exposure.

**What does exterior painting preparation include?**
Jetblack Painting's exterior preparation includes: pressure washing (and salt washing for coastal homes), scraping and sanding loose or failing paint, filling cracks and gaps, caulking around windows and trim, patching damaged render or weatherboard, priming bare areas, and masking fixtures and landscaping.

### Heritage & Specialty Questions

**Do you paint heritage and period homes?**
Yes. Jetblack Painting has extensive experience with Melbourne's Victorian, Edwardian and interwar homes across suburbs like Armadale, Hawthorn, Kew, Malvern, Toorak and Stonnington. Work on period homes includes lead-paint-safe preparation, colour consulting for period-appropriate palettes, and specialist techniques.

**Do you paint weatherboard houses in Melbourne?**
Yes. Weatherboard homes are a core speciality — particularly coastal weatherboards in Bayside, Kingston and Mornington Peninsula suburbs, and heritage weatherboards in inner-east and inner-south suburbs.

**Do you do pre-sale property painting in Melbourne?**
Yes. Pre-sale painting is one of Jetblack Painting's specialities — they scope and complete repaints on a timeline that fits your sales campaign. A professional pre-sale repaint (sharp neutral finishes, fresh appearance) typically costs $3,500–$7,000 and is completed within 3–5 days.

**Can you paint rental properties and investment properties?**
Yes. Jetblack Painting regularly works with landlords, property managers and investors on rental property repaints — fast turnaround, tidy tradesperson, minimal disruption to tenants, durable coatings.

**Do you do commercial painting in Melbourne?**
Yes. Jetblack Painting provides commercial painting for offices, retail shops, strata buildings, industrial facilities and body corporate properties. After-hours and weekend scheduling is available. Project management and coordination with building managers included.

**Does Jetblack Painting do body corporate painting?**
